Spec.summary: The candidate only aligns a controlled one-tick late-fault fixture with the existing bounded append-order recovery scan. Opaque attempt-ID lexical ordering cannot choose the first rowid item reliably. The new first-append selection and exact failure-key/no-binding checks strengthen fault attribution for a future run while preserving every original rollback count guard, safe import preview, old grade/audit/manual-review byte comparison, recovery of other two grades and FK integrity. No production recovery, history, Policy, migration or HTTP/DTO behavior changes. Both complete evidence modules are selected at exact reviewed test blobs. The original actual integration3FAIL and unknown extra-event identity remain unresolved historical facts; this source review does not close them or claim corrected runtime success.

fixture_and_owner_contract.source_limits: Rowid ordering is an internal owned-fixture alignment, not a new externally visible product contract. This review does not prove that every possible workspace or fault order is covered.
fixture_and_owner_contract.why_narrow: The source selects the first appended grade that this current one-workspace fixture will offer to the first bounded recovery tick. It does not change production sorting, grade IDs, arbitrary owner behavior or source records.

limitations: Spec source review and strict AST/byte/source checks are not corrected runtime PASS or closure of the original full integration gate.
The actual extra event was not attributed in the original log; no source-only causal verdict is promoted.
Parallel Standards review remains separate; this report does not fabricate its conclusion.

new_assertions.exact_failure_key: After actual first dispatch tick, entire failure-key list must equal [selected_first_grade_key], not merely count1.

new_assertions.why_meaningful: A trigger that misses the first processed grade, targets a different grade, commits a binding for the faulted grade or loses failure identity will still fail this future test. Original global count guard is not relaxed to accommodate an unexplained event.
